A diamond color chart grades white diamonds from **D (completely colorless)** to **Z (light yellow or brown)** using the standard scale created by the [GIA 4Cs Color Scale](https://www.gia.edu/gia-about/4cs-color).[[1]](https://www.gia.edu/gia-about/4cs-color)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/)

### GIA Diamond Color Scale and Categories

- **D – F (Colorless):** 
	- **Appearance:** Extremely rare and icy white with no detectable color.
	- **Value:** Highest price and rarity.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/)[[2]](https://www.rarecarat.com/education/color/what-is-the-diamond-color-chart)[[3]](https://www.whiteflash.com/diamond-education/diamond-color/)
- **G – J (Near Colorless):** 
	- **Appearance:** Very subtle traces of warmth that are hard to see with the naked eye, especially when set in jewelry.
	- **Value:** Great balance of beauty and budget.[[1]](https://www.rarecarat.com/education/color/what-is-the-diamond-color-chart)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/)
- **K – M (Faint Color):** 
	- **Appearance:** A faint yellow or warm tint that can be seen without a magnifier.
	- **Value:** More affordable and works well with yellow or rose gold settings.[[1]](https://www.gabrielny.com/blog/diamond-color/)[[2]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/)[[3]](https://www.rarecarat.com/education/color/what-is-the-diamond-color-chart)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tLdOXsRJ3IA&t=11)
- **N – R (Very Light Color):** 
	- **Appearance:** A noticeable yellow or brownish hue.
	- **Value:** Lower price point.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/)[[2]](https://www.rarecarat.com/education/color/what-is-the-diamond-color-chart)
- **S – Z (Light Color):** 
	- **Appearance:** Strong, clearly visible yellow or brown tint.
	- **Value:** Most accessible pricing.[[1]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/)

*(Note: Diamonds with color grades past Z or featuring deep natural tones like pink or blue are classified separately as "fancy colored diamonds".)* You can learn more about how different retailers evaluate these grades through guides like [Brilliant Earth's Diamond Color Scale](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/).[[1]](https://www.gia.edu/gia-about/4cs-color)[[2]](https://www.windsorfinejewelers.com/diamond/education/color)[[3]](https://www.brilliantearth.com/guides/diamond-color/)If you'd like, let me know:

- What **metal type** you plan to use for the ring (platinum, yellow gold, etc.)
- The target **diamond shape** or **carat size** 

I can help you pick the best color grade that looks colorless to the eye while saving you money.
